# Platform Prism

> Every platform decision, proved before it ships.

A white-label Prism for teams that run content-addressed platforms: registries, VM images, air-gapped sites and the rollouts that depend on them. Each decision the platform makes is a small app whose rules are proved in Lean, compiled to one verified artifact, and run in your browser.

## Views

- [Platform engineering](./platform/index.html): Can my teams build on this registry, and on these addresses? (Platform engineer, technical)
- [Cloud engineering](./cloud/index.html): Will my images and disks arrive whole, here and at the disconnected site? (Cloud engineer, technical)
- [Operations and SRE](./operator/index.html): What does the registry keep, and what can I safely reclaim tonight? (Registry operator, technical)
- [Security and supply chain](./security/index.html): Can anything unsigned, tampered or from the wrong place ever run? (Security engineer, technical)
- [Engineering leadership](./leader/index.html): Are we ready to roll out? Go, hold or no-go. (Engineering leader, non-technical)
- [Business and risk](./business/index.html): What are we paying for, and what could we lose? (Business owner, non-technical)

## Decision apps

- conformance-verdict: Tell a platform team, from one run of the kappa-conformance binary, whether their registry is ideal, conformant or not, and what exit code CI sees. Request fields: config network must should. Answers: ideal, conformant, nonconformant, config-error, network-error.
- kappa-label-check: Decide if a string is a well-formed kappa-label, the content address every kappa-distribution object is named by, before anything trusts it. Request fields: axis colons hex digits. Answers: permit, deny, not-applicable, indeterminate.
- upload-session: Give the next state of a chunked blob upload to a kappa-distribution registry, so a client always knows whether to send, resume, retry or stop. Request fields: state event label. Answers: open, receiving, committed, rejected, abandoned.
- gc-eviction: Decide whether garbage collection may evict a blob from a kappa-distribution registry, so storage is reclaimed without losing anything a tag, pin, finalizer or upload still needs. Request fields: tag pin finalizer upload. Answers: retain, evict.
- vm-image-admission: Decide if a KubeVirt VM image distributed as an OCI artifact may run on a platform cluster, including an air-gapped one. Request fields: signature digest arch source site verifier. Answers: permit, deny, not-applicable, indeterminate.
- rollout-gate: Tell an engineering leader, in one word, whether a content-addressed platform is ready to roll out: go, hold or no-go. Request fields: conformance key backup env images. Answers: go, hold, no-go.

## Words

- content address: a fingerprint of the bytes: same bytes, same name, anywhere. Technically: digest, as in image@sha256:....
- kappa-label: the written form of that fingerprint. Technically: algorithm:hex, such as sha256:<64 hex digits>.
- canonical form: the one agreed way to write something, so everyone fingerprints the same thing. Technically: the exact bytes a digest is taken over.
- holo: the packaged decision, sealed so nobody can quietly change it. Technically: a verified WebAssembly artifact with its fingerprint and acceptance vectors.
- property: a promise that is checked by a machine for every case, not sampled by tests. Technically: a theorem the Lean kernel checks for every possible request.
- verify: the page checks the seal before it answers you. Technically: check the fingerprint and replay every acceptance vector before answering.
- facet: one side of the same object, written for one kind of reader. Technically: one generated view of the model: architecture, design, security, quality, compliance, release.
